change.title: ao-replay/8832-r2
change.description: fix(chat): say the "@" files are loading, and don't refetch after leaving
change.author: Dhruv Sharma

contracts.action: Show a "Loading files…" note in the composer menu while the first `@` file-path list loads, and let Escape dismiss it
contracts.equivalent_path: The existing `skillsNote` / "Loading skills…" path at ChatComposer.tsx:874 and its Escape handling at ChatComposer.tsx:2268-2275
contracts.before_after: The new path matches the skills path. It is gated on the trigger kind and on `trigger.key !== dismissedKey`, and it feeds `menuShown` and `loadingNote`. Escape sets `dismissedKeyRef` and `dismissedKey` exactly as the skills branch does. The `@` trigger is detected by the editor independently of `filePaths`, so the note can show with an empty list. The query's `isLoading` only becomes true once `fileMenuAsked` has enabled the query, so there is at most one render with no note before it appears.
contracts.visible_effect: Typing `@` the first time in a session shows "Loading files…" instead of nothing. The note disappears when paths arrive or the user presses Escape.
contracts.failure_mode: If the path fetch fails (`retry: false`), `isLoading` goes false and the menu stays closed, which is the same silent state as before the change. Surfaces that do not pass `filePathsLoading` (Cloud chat) default to false and are unchanged.

contracts.action: Open the Files inspector with `queryClient.prefetchQuery` instead of `void fetchWorkspaceFiles()`
contracts.equivalent_path: `fetchWorkspaceFiles` at SessionView.tsx:2446-2452 (`fetchQuery` plus one retry after a cancelled fetch), which is still used at lines 2286 and 2557
contracts.before_after: Both calls use the same options and query key, and the options set no `staleTime`. Both therefore fetch when the data is stale and reuse it otherwise. The differences are that `prefetchQuery` swallows rejections (the old `void fetchQuery` could raise an unhandled rejection) and does not retry after a cancellation. The Files inspector's own `useQuery` on the same key is what the user sees.
contracts.visible_effect: No visible change. The cache is warmed on the Files click, and a failed prefetch no longer produces an unhandled rejection.
contracts.failure_mode: A failed or cancelled prefetch is silent here. The inspector's `useQuery` on the same key surfaces the error, so nothing is lost.

summary: I found nothing to flag in this part. The "Loading files…" note mirrors the existing "Loading skills…" path: same gating on the trigger kind and dismissed key, and the same Escape handling. The new `filePathsLoading` prop is wired through `SessionChatSurface` and `ChatWorkspace` into `ChatComposer`, and surfaces that don't pass it default to false. The `SessionView` switch to `prefetchQuery` uses the same query options and key as `fetchWorkspaceFiles`. The only behaviour changes are that rejections are swallowed and there is no retry after a cancelled fetch, and the inspector's own `useQuery` still reports errors. The `useConversation.ts` change moves the JSDoc from `fetchWorkspaceFilePaths` to `useWorkspaceFilePaths`, which fixes a misattached comment. The new test follows the skills-loading test's pattern. The PR title says "don't refetch after leaving", but I found no change in this diff that does that. The `prefetchQuery` swap doesn't change staleness, since the query options set no `staleTime`. The `staleTime` setting that decides refetch-on-return may be outside this diff, so I couldn't confirm that part of the claim. I did not read any code outside this part's files to check it.
